blocks.content: The 74th Amendment Act of 1992 has given constitutional status to the urban local bodies and brought them under the purview of justiciable part of the Constitution.

items: Articles 243-ZD (District Planning Committee) and 243-ZE (Metropolitan Planning Committee) are key provisions frequently asked in competitive exams.
In case of premature dissolution, fresh elections must be conducted within 6 months, and the new body continues only for the remainder of the 5-year period.
The 12th Schedule explicitly enumerates 18 functional matters assigned to Municipalities under Article 243-W.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: The 74th Constitutional Amendment Act of 1992 accorded constitutional status to Urban Local Bodies (ULBs) and came into force on June 1, 1993.
It inserted Part IX-A titled 'The Municipalities' (Articles 243-P to 243-ZG) and the 12th Schedule containing 18 functional items.
Creates a three-type system of urban local government: Nagar Panchayat, Municipal Council, and Municipal Corporation.
Mandates direct elections for all members of a municipality and fixed 5-year terms.
Provides for mandatory reservation of not less than one-third of total seats for women, including SC/ST women.
